import pandas as pd

# Load the time_series_data.csv dataset
df_time_series = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')

# Extract the 'CE' and 'Depot' columns
ce_values = df_time_series['CE']
depot_values = df_time_series['Depot']

# Identify the index of the maximum 'Depot' value
max_depot_index = depot_values.idxmax()

# Find the corresponding 'CE' value
peak_ce = ce_values[max_depot_index]

# Determine the century
peak_century = peak_ce // 100

peak_century

import pandas as pd

# Load the time_series_data.csv dataset
df_time_series = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')

# Interpolate missing values in the 'Depot' column using linear interpolation
df_time_series['Depot_interpolated'] = df_time_series['Depot'].interpolate(method='linear')

# Calculate a rolling mean of the interpolated 'Depot' values with a window size of 100
rolling_mean = df_time_series['Depot_interpolated'].rolling(window=100).mean()

# Identify the index of the maximum rolling mean value
max_rolling_mean_index = rolling_mean.idxmax()

# Find the corresponding 'CE' value
peak_ce_rolling_mean = df_time_series['CE'][max_rolling_mean_index]

# Determine the century
peak_century_rolling_mean = peak_ce_rolling_mean // 100

peak_century_rolling_mean
